common_name: Zinderella Zinnia (Scabiosa-Flowered Novelty Cut Flower Series)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost in warm soil; Zinderella bears distinctive scabiosa-form flowers with a raised, pincushion-like center surrounded by a single row of outer petals.

directions: Direct sow after frost in warm, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Zinderella is a novelty zinnia series bred for a distinctive scabiosa-flowered form, in which a domed, pincushion-like center of small tubular florets is ringed by a single row of larger outer petals, giving each bloom a layered, two-tiered look quite different from the classic double zinnia. Colors across the series range through soft peach, lilac, and purple tones popular with cut-flower growers and florists for their unusual texture. The tall, sturdy stems make excellent, long-lasting cut flowers, and regular cutting or deadheading keeps plants producing new blooms over a long summer season. Like other zinnias it thrives in heat and draws bees and butterflies heavily; good air circulation helps reduce powdery mildew in humid climates.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
